label: Chios

names.text: The alternative names are as given in the item's known list, from the Wikipedia article on the breed; not separately confirmed on a second page.

about.text: The Chios is a Greek sheep breed commonly accepted to have originated on the island of Chios. It is kept on the Greek mainland as well as on the island, and its milk is used for feta, batzos and manouri cheeses.

sources.text: Origin on Chios and the cheeses from Wikipedia; mainland keeping from Amalthia, which says most surviving pure and crossed animals are now kept on the Greek mainland.

origin.place: The island of Chios, Greece; formed from crosses of autochthonous sheep, possibly with Karaman or Daglic fat-tailed sheep

sources.text: Place and possible crossings from Amalthia; the Wikipedia article says the breed's origins are unknown but commonly accepted to be Chios. No year of formation was found.

Population figure of 51,860 in 2007 as the article gives it, per DAD-IS; the article does not name the country the count covers, so GR is taken from the breed's home. Found in the fetched page text, not on DAD-IS itself.

Purebred population of 128,500 animals per 2019 data from the 'Chios Sheep Breeders-Macedonia' cooperation, as quoted on Amalthia. The cooperation's name points to northern Greece, but the country is not stated, so GR is an assumption.

Per lactation 265 to 600 lb (120 to 272 kg) as the article gives it, citing Oklahoma State University; a 2010 Greek farm survey average of 276.6 kg per ewe adjusted to 210 days, giving the max of 277; the average lactation is 210 days (the record lactation of 777 litres in 220 days is in facts, not here). The survey is dated 2010 on the page. Oklahoma State and the Greek survey are not opened here; the figures are as the article reports them.
The article describes the breed as primarily dairy, with the milk used for feta, batzos and manouri; lambs are reared for 6 to 8 weeks but it is not described as a meat breed.

facts.v: The record is 777 litres in a 220-day lactation.

sources.text: Stated in the article's yield section, without a named source on the page as fetched.

facts.v: Already well known in the 1940s for high milk productivity and large litters; a 1950 Ministry of Agriculture milk-monitoring programme followed.
In the mid-1960s, 2,800 ewes were monitored on Chios; fewer than 300 animals remained on the island at the time of the page.

sources.text: From Amalthia's history section; the page's date for 'presently' is not stated.

gaps: Milk composition (fat, protein, lactose, solids) not found on Wikipedia or Amalthia; the Oklahoma State and DAD-IS breed pages were not reachable (Oklahoma State returned 403, DAD-IS breed pages are dynamic and not found by search). No year of formation found. Risk status: Amalthia lists the breed as 'Not at Risk' with no year and no DAD-IS reference, so it is left out; the DAD-IS status could not be confirmed. Country of the 2007 DAD-IS count is not stated in the source.
